videos.title: Heatstroke
videos.description: A medical emergency. The body’s core temperature rises above about 40 °C and its cooling system fails. Without fast cooling it can kill or cause lasting organ damage.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat exhaustion
videos.description: The warning stage before heatstroke: heavy sweating, weakness, dizziness and nausea. Rest, water and cooling usually bring recovery.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat stress
videos.description: When the body takes in or makes more heat than it can shed, from hot air, humidity, sun and physical work.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Limits to adaptation
videos.description: The point beyond which adjusting no longer prevents harm. Places used to heat cope better with days of 30–35 °C, but a study of 2.7 million firms found no adaptation to days above 40 °C.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Acclimatisation
videos.description: The body slowly adjusting to heat over one to two weeks. New and returning workers are most at risk until it has.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Excess deaths
videos.description: Deaths above the normal number for that place and time of year. Because death certificates rarely say “heat”, this is how the real toll of a heatwave is counted.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Wet-bulb temperature

videos.title: Dry heat and humid heat
videos.description: Dry heat is high temperature with low humidity: sweat still evaporates, but the body soaks up heat fast. It peaks in South Asia’s pre-monsoon months.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Cool roof
videos.description: A roof painted or built to reflect sunlight, so less heat reaches the room below.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Refrigerant
videos.description: The fluid inside air conditioners and fridges that carries heat away. Many common ones are powerful greenhouse gases if they leak.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Black carbon
videos.description: Soot from diesel, wood, coal and brick kilns. It warms the air, and when it settles on snow and ice it darkens them so they melt faster.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Vicious cycle
videos.description: A harm that feeds itself: each turn of the loop makes the next one worse. This map shows where those loops could be interrupted.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Maladaptation
videos.description: A response to heat that makes things worse elsewhere or later, such as air conditioners that cool a room but heat the street.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Mean radiant temperature
videos.description: The heat your body takes in from the sun and from hot surfaces around it: roads, walls and roofs. In strong sun it shapes how hot you feel more than air temperature does, which is why shade matters so much.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Thermal comfort
videos.description: How hot or cold a person feels. It depends on air temperature, humidity, wind, sun, clothing and activity, not on air temperature alone.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Albedo
videos.description: How much sunlight a surface reflects. A white roof has a high albedo and stays cooler; dark asphalt has a low albedo and stores heat.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Evapotranspiration
videos.description: Water evaporating from soil and leaves. It draws heat out of the air, so well-watered plants cool their surroundings. Plants short of water stop cooling.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Nature-based solutions
videos.description: Using living systems such as trees, wetlands, soils and water to tackle problems like heat and flooding while also benefiting people and nature.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Ecosystem services
videos.description: The benefits people get from nature: shade and cooling, cleaner air and water, rain soaking into the ground, food and places to rest.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Blue-green infrastructure
videos.description: A network of water (blue) and plants and soil (green), such as rivers, ponds, wetlands, parks and planted drains, designed to manage rain and heat together.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Grey infrastructure
videos.description: Engineered, mostly concrete systems such as pipes, drains, embankments and pumps. Many good solutions mix grey and green.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Sponge city
videos.description: A city designed to soak up, store, clean and slowly release rainwater through parks, wetlands, permeable ground and planted drains, not only pipes.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Co-benefits
videos.description: The extra gains a measure brings beyond its main aim, such as a park built to hold floodwater that also cools the street and gives children somewhere to play.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Ecosystem-based adaptation
videos.description: Using nature to help people adapt to climate change, such as mangroves against storm surges or trees for shade. A kind of nature-based solution.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Green gentrification
videos.description: When a new park or greening raises rents and land prices so much that the poorer residents it was meant to help are pushed out.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Environmental justice
videos.description: A fair share of environmental benefits and harms, and a fair say in decisions about them. Poorer neighbourhoods are often hotter and less green.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Aquifer
videos.description: Underground layers of rock or sand that hold groundwater, the water that wells and pumps draw from.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Agroforestry
videos.description: Growing trees alongside crops or livestock. The trees shade the soil, help it hold moisture and give farmers another source of income.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Chief heat officer
videos.description: A city official whose job is heat: joining up health, water, power, schools and work so that protection is planned before the hot season. Dhaka North City Corporation appointed Asia’s first in 2023.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat alert levels
videos.description: Graded warnings, such as caution, danger and extreme danger, set at levels of heat that harm health locally. A good plan ties each level to named actions, so a warning switches protection on.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Work–rest cycle
videos.description: Building shaded rest into each hour of hot, heavy work. In Singapore, employers must give at least 10 minutes’ shaded rest each hour for heavy outdoor work at a wet-bulb globe temperature of 32 °C or more.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Ward-level heat plan
videos.description: A heat action plan that maps risk neighbourhood by neighbourhood, using felt heat, warm nights and who lives there, so help goes first where risk is highest. Thane, next to Mumbai, built its 2024 plan this way.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Core elements of a heat plan
videos.description: WHO/Europe’s checklist for a complete heat–health action plan: governance, a warning system, people at risk, communication, a resilient health system, reducing exposure, surveillance, and monitoring and learning.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Climate attribution
videos.description: Working out how much climate change has added to an event or its harm. The 2026 Lancet Countdown attributes 71.5% of 2023’s heat deaths to climate change, and 11.3 of 13.5 heatwave days per person in 2025.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Undercounted heat deaths
videos.description: Heat deaths that are never recorded as heat deaths, because certificates name the immediate cause, such as a heart attack.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Lost work hours
videos.description: Work that heat makes unsafe or impossible. The 2026 Lancet Countdown estimates 573 billion potential work hours were lost to heat in 2025, with farm workers losing twice as many hours as any other sector.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Informal work
videos.description: Work without a formal contract, sick pay or social insurance, often outdoors: street vending, construction, farm and home-based work.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat and learning
videos.description: Lost schooling when heat closes schools or makes classrooms too hot to learn in. In April 2024, Bangladesh closed schools for about 33 million children, and 5,288 schools in the Philippines moved to remote learning.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The cooling gap
videos.description: The difference between people who can stay cool and those who can’t. Air conditioning may have prevented about 360,000 deaths a year in 2022 and 2023, but only about 3% of households in the poorest countries have it.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Cooling demand
videos.description: How much cooling people need, and the energy it takes. Southeast Asia’s air conditioners could rise from about 40 million to 300 million by 2040, half of them in Indonesia.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Peak power demand
videos.description: The highest electricity load of the day or year, which in hot countries comes with heat and air conditioning.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Glacier loss
videos.description: Mountain ice shrinking faster than snow can replace it. In the Hindu Kush Himalaya, glaciers lost ice 65% faster in the 2010s than in the decade before, and could lose 30–50% of their volume by 2100.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Peat fires
videos.description: Fires that smoulder in drained peatland, the thick, wet soil of tropical swamps. Once dry, peat burns underground for weeks and fills the air with haze.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Hot nights and crops
videos.description: Crops need cool nights too. At the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines, rice yields fell about 10% for each 1 °C rise in growing-season night temperature.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Adaptation finance gap
videos.description: The difference between what countries say they need to adapt to climate change and the money that arrives.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat and credit
videos.description: How heat travels from wages to lenders: lost working hours mean missed repayments, and lenders face a cash crunch. About 60% of India’s ₹3.81 trillion microfinance portfolio is in farming and allied work.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Older people and heat
videos.description: With age, thirst fades and the body sweats less, so it cools more slowly and the heart works harder.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat in pregnancy
videos.description: A pregnant body runs warm and has less room to cool. Each 1 °C rise raises the odds of a preterm birth by about 5%, and a heatwave by about 16%.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Babies and young children in heat
videos.description: Babies and small children overheat and lose water faster than adults, and depend on someone else to notice. In 2014–2023, each infant in India faced an average of 7.7 heatwave days a year, 47% more than in the 1990s.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat, kidneys and the heart
videos.description: Sweating and dehydration make the heart work harder and can damage the kidneys, especially with repeated exposure. People already living with heart, kidney or lung conditions have less room to cope.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Sleep in the heat
videos.description: To fall asleep, the body needs to cool. On hot nights sleep comes later and ends sooner, so the next day starts already depleted. A study of 47,628 people’s sleep wristbands in 68 countries found hot nights cut sleep.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat and the mind
videos.description: Heat is linked to more anxiety, distress and suicide, and to worse outcomes for people living with mental illness.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: When home is hotter than outside
videos.description: Thin metal roofs, small windows and crowded rooms can make a home hotter inside than out, worst at night. In Ahmedabad, people in informal settlements faced temperatures up to 7.6 °C higher than people in formal housing.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Kitchen heat
videos.description: Cooking over a fire in a small, smoky kitchen during a heatwave: a daily ‘thermal labour’ that falls hardest on women in the poorest single-room homes.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat illness first aid
videos.description: Heatstroke is an emergency, and cooling buys time: move the person to shade, cool them with water and fanning, call for help, and give small sips of water only if they are awake.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat check-ins
videos.description: A call or a knock for people who live alone or can’t easily leave home. In Chicago’s 1995 heatwave, living alone and not leaving home were among the strongest risks of dying.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat in closed places
videos.description: Prisons, hostels, care homes and crowded shelters, where people can’t leave for shade. Tamil Nadu’s heat strategy names prisoners among the groups it is meant to reach, and proposes cool roofs and trees for its jails.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Clinics in a heatwave
videos.description: Heatwaves bring surges of patients just as staff, power and supplies are under strain. In 2024, Indian hospitals prepared heatstroke rooms, ice baths and cooled beds before the peak.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Warning the hospitals first
videos.description: A heat warning that reaches clinics a day or two early, so they can add staff, stock fluids and clear beds.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Cold chains in the heat
videos.description: Every fridge and cool box from the factory to the patient or the plate. Without reliable power, fridges for food, medicines and vaccines fail; 526 million tonnes of food are lost each year for lack of refrigeration.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: When phones go quiet
videos.description: Phone masts and networks need power and cooling too. In Bangladesh in 2026, mobile signals weakened as blackouts spread; warnings, mobile payments and calls for help all ride on them.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Power grids in a heatwave
videos.description: Demand peaks as everyone switches on cooling, just as hot lines and transformers struggle. An early World Bank estimate put the cost of northern Viet Nam’s power cuts in May and June 2023 at US$1.4 billion.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Water for power, power for water
videos.description: Many power plants need water to cool, and water pumps need power to run, so in a heatwave each strains the other. In 2016, India lost 14 TWh of electricity because thermal power plants ran short of water.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The diesel fallback
videos.description: When the grid fails, homes, shops and hospitals that can afford it switch to diesel generators, which keep the lights on and add to the heat and the smoke.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: City trees under heat
videos.description: Heat, drought and missing upkeep can kill street trees just when their shade is needed. Across 164 cities, 56% of urban tree and shrub species already face temperatures beyond their natural range, and 76% could by 2050.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Shade follows wealth
videos.description: Trees and parks cluster in better-off neighbourhoods, which can pay for them and their upkeep, so poorer districts stay hotter.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Cool classrooms
videos.description: A hot classroom is hard to learn in, and when it becomes unsafe, schools close. In 2024, heatwaves disrupted the schooling of 171 million students; South Asia was the most affected region.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Roads and rails in the heat
videos.description: Steel rails expand and can buckle, so trains slow; roads soften; hot, thin air means planes need longer runways. Journeys, shifts and supplies, including medicines and food, are delayed.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: When dry soil heats the air
videos.description: Moist soil cools the air as its water evaporates. When soil dries, that cooling stops, so the air heats faster and dries the soil further: a loop that water kept in the ground can break.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Asia’s last tropical ice
videos.description: On Puncak Jaya in Papua, Indonesia, 99% of the glacier area has gone since 1850. About 0.17 km² was left in 2024, and it will very likely disappear around 2030.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Heat, drought and salt water
videos.description: Heat and drought lower rivers and canals, and the sea pushes inland. In Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta in February 2024, farmers who pumped salty canal water onto their rice lost up to half their crop.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The global cooling loop
videos.description: Cooling powered by fossil fuels adds to the warming that makes us need more cooling.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The dry-soil loop
videos.description: Heat dries the soil. Dry soil can’t cool itself, so the land heats up faster.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The melting-ice loop
videos.description: Heat melts ice. Darker ground and water absorb more sunlight, and the melting speeds up.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The wildfire loop
videos.description: Heat dries forests into fuel. Fires release carbon and strip away the trees that cool the land.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The cooling trap
videos.description: Air conditioning heats the street, and a hotter city needs even more air conditioning.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The energy–water loop
videos.description: Water systems need power and power plants need water. In a heatwave, each failure deepens the other.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The groundwater loop
videos.description: Dry fields need more water, so farmers pump harder, aquifers fall and the shortage deepens.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The dying-green loop
videos.description: Heat and drought kill city trees. Without their shade the streets get hotter, and hotter streets kill more trees.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The overwhelmed-clinic loop
videos.description: Heat illness floods clinics. Overwhelmed clinics treat people later, and more cases become severe.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The poverty–heat trap
videos.description: People who can’t afford to stop working fall ill. Illness costs income, and lost income makes stopping even less affordable.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The medical-debt trap
videos.description: Treatment costs push families into debt. Debt removes any option to rest, and working through the heat brings more illness.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The energy-poverty trap
videos.description: People who can’t afford to cool fall ill. Illness brings debt, and debt puts cooling even further out of reach.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The displacement loop
videos.description: People forced to move often land in heat-trapping housing, fall ill, lose income, fall further behind, and are forced to move again.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The lost-schooling loop
videos.description: Children pulled out of school earn less as adults, and poorer families pull more children out of school.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The sleepless-nights loop
videos.description: Hot nights wreck sleep. Poor sleep frays mental health, and stress makes sleep harder still.

videos.title: The green-displacement loop
videos.description: Green space follows wealth. When greening reaches poorer districts without protection, rents rise, residents are pushed into hotter housing, and the gap grows.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The heat credit squeeze
videos.description: Heat empties shops and small firms miss repayments. Banks tighten credit, so firms can’t afford to adapt, and the next heatwave hits harder.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The farm-debt loop
videos.description: A failed harvest pushes farmers into debt. Debt leaves less for seed, water and fertiliser, so the next harvest fails more easily.

videos.title: The invisible-deaths loop
videos.description: Heat deaths go uncounted, so heat protection goes unfunded, so more people die uncounted.

videos.title: The reactive-spending loop
videos.description: Stretched budgets skimp on prevention. Emergencies multiply, and costly emergency response stretches budgets further.

videos.title: The protection-gap loop
videos.description: As insurers retreat, public budgets absorb the losses, protection is cut, and the risk drives insurers further away.

videos.title: 02:00: The night that never cools
videos.description: A garment worker in Dhaka. It is two in the morning and her tin-roofed room is still holding the day’s heat. She has barely slept, her body hasn’t recovered from yesterday, and the shift starts at seven.

videos.title: 06:00: Salt in the canal
videos.description: A rice farmer in Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta. Before dawn he checks the canal beside his rice. The heat has drawn it low, and the water tastes of salt.

videos.title: 09:00: The field can’t wait
videos.description: A woman farming rainfed land in Nepal’s Madhesh plains. The monsoon is late, and by mid-morning her seedlings are wilting. The seed was bought on credit, so if this crop fails the debt grows.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: 12:00: School closes
videos.description: A girl in rural Bangladesh. Her school shuts for the heat again. At home she fetches water and looks after her younger brothers, and after weeks like this her family starts to wonder whether she should go back at all.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: 13:00: No shade between orders
videos.description: A delivery rider in Jakarta. At midday the road shimmers and the delivery app keeps sending orders. He is paid by the delivery, so every rest in the shade costs him money. Tonight, his rented room has no fan.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: 15:00: The grid gives way
videos.description: A city at its peak. Every air conditioner is running. The grid fails, water pumps stop and the district clinic loses its cooling just as heat cases arrive.

videos.title: 18:00: The bill arrives
videos.description: A street food vendor in Bangkok. Her stock spoiled in the heat, and her husband’s treatment for heat exhaustion last week was paid with a loan. Tomorrow she has to work longer.

videos.title: 22:00: A death no one counts
videos.description: An older man living alone in Chennai. He dies at home in a room that stayed hot all day. His death certificate will say heart failure, so it never shows up as a heat death.

videos.title: Heat has no single owner
videos.description: Heat sits between health, disaster, labour and urban departments, so no single department holds the mandate or the budget line.

videos.title: Money arrives after the emergency
videos.description: Budgets are drawn up for relief, not prevention, and short political cycles reward a visible response over quiet risk reduction.

videos.title: Heat stays invisible
videos.description: Deaths are recorded as heart or kidney failure, local risk is not mapped, and heat feels like normal weather rather than an emergency.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: Too few people know how
videos.description: Plans are often prepared with outside experts, and district teams may not get the training, time or handover they need when staff move on.

videos.title: Guidance not yet binding
videos.description: Advice exists, but rest breaks, building codes and cooling standards are often voluntary or rarely inspected.
videos.rights: The site’s text, data, films and illustrations are shared under CC BY 4.0: credit “Common Shade” with a link to https://beattheheat.asia, and say if you made changes.

videos.title: The people at risk aren’t in the room
videos.description: Plans are often made without hearing from women, outdoor workers, older people, people with disabilities or migrants, so warnings and shelters miss them.

videos.title: Good solutions stay small
videos.description: Cool roofs, efficient cooling and heat insurance work in pilots, but prices stay high, standards are missing and finance does not follow.
